newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: NORWEGIAN FUNDS,NOMURA MIGHT BUY IN LITIMPEKS.
newsitem.headline: NORWEGIAN FUNDS,NOMURA MIGHT BUY IN LITIMPEKS.

text.p: Three Norwegian funds and Nomura Securities intend to acquire the major part of the new 60 million litas share issue of Lithuania's Litimpeks Bank, the newspaper Verslo Zinios reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper sources said that Norways's Baltic Investment Fund, Baltic Partners, and Baltic Eiedam and Hotel were eyeing the troubled bank.
The newspaper sources also said that 10 percent of the issue might be offered to Poland's Kredyt Bank S.A. and no new investor should acquire more than 10 percent of the issue.
Verslo Zinios' sources said that the bank signed an agreement with Norwegian fund Balticum Managment to become a financial advisor and to distribute Litimpeks' share issue abroad.
The manager of Balticum Managment Magne Reme neither denied nor confirmed this, the paper said.
It added that Litimpeks officials declined to comment.
The bank confirmed earlier that it was in talks with Estonia's Tallinna Pank and Poland's Kredyt Bank.
Litimpeks Bank was unexpectedly closed at the end of 1995 when the country was hit by a severe banking crisis but was reopened in June of 1996.
The bank posted losses of 6.3 million litas in 1996 and 1.9 million litas losses in the first quarter of 1997.
